title: Doughnut Economics City Portrait
description: Schema for a city/region doughnut economics portrait. 12 standard social foundations + 9 standard ecological ceilings, each optionally extended with locally-defined dimensions (e.g. 'mobility' for Petaluma and NYC; 'waste & materials' for both; 'heat & climate resilience' for NYC). Supports DEAL's four-lens City Portrait method: the required per-dimension fields carry the LOCAL lens (local-social for social dimensions, local-ecological for ecological ones) and the optional 'global' block carries the GLOBAL lens (global-social / global-ecological). Also supports sub-jurisdiction disaggregation via the optional 'boroughs' block, used by the NYC portrait to carry all five boroughs per dimension.

jurisdictionType.description: What kind of jurisdiction this portrait describes. Borough portraits are derived from a parent city portrait.

parentId.description: For a sub-jurisdiction portrait (jurisdictionType 'borough'), the meta.id of the parent city portrait it was derived from.

subJurisdictions.description: For a city portrait carrying disaggregated data, the keys used in each dimension's 'boroughs' block, e.g. ['bronx','brooklyn','manhattan','queens','statenIsland'].

lenses.description: Which of DEAL's four City Portrait lenses this portrait populates. A local-only portrait lists the two local lenses; a full four-lens portrait lists all four.

policyAnchor.description: The planning or policy process this portrait is anchored to, e.g. 'Petaluma General Plan update' or 'Local Law 97 / PlaNYC / City of Yes'.

social.description: 12 standard social foundation dimensions, optionally with locally-defined additions (e.g. 'mobility')

ecological.description: 9 standard ecological ceiling dimensions, optionally with locally-defined additions (e.g. 'waste & materials', 'heat & climate resilience')

confidence.description: high=primary source, current, correct geographic scale; medium=primary but older or wrong scale, or good secondary; low=proxy, unverified, or source fetch failed

geographicScale.description: Geographic level the data is actually reported at. Never label a metro or state figure as 'city'.

productionVsConsumption.description: For ecological indicators: whether the figure counts impacts occurring inside the jurisdiction (production-based) or embodied in what the jurisdiction consumes (consumption-based).

subJurisdictionEntry.description: One sub-jurisdiction's (e.g. borough's) reading for this dimension. A null value with a populated 'note' is the correct representation of a genuine data gap — never interpolate or pro-rate a citywide figure.

note.description: Required when value is null: why the figure is unavailable at this scale and what the closest proxy or holder of the data is.

lensEntry.description: A single lens reading for a dimension. Used for the optional 'global' block.

levelRationale.description: Why this level, tied explicitly to the stated target.

boroughs.description: Sub-jurisdiction disaggregation measured on THIS lens's basis. Used where borough data exists only for the global/consumption-based accounting and not for the local/production-based one (e.g. NYC's Consumption-Based Emissions Inventory). Never mix bases between local.boroughs and global.boroughs.

lens.description: Which local lens the top-level fields of this dimension represent. Defaults by ring: social dimensions are local-social, ecological dimensions are local-ecological.

levelRationale.description: One or two sentences justifying the level against the stated target. Expected in practice for any non-null level.

value.description: The actual data value with units

productionVsConsumptionNote.description: Free-text qualification of the production/consumption basis, where the enum alone loses information (e.g. 'consumption-based; framing only, not quantified for this city').

boroughs.description: Sub-jurisdiction disaggregation for this dimension. Keys should match meta.subJurisdictions.

neighborhoodNote.description: The sharpest intra-jurisdiction disparity for this dimension, with named places and sourced values.

global.description: The global lens for this dimension: global-social for social dimensions, global-ecological for ecological ones. What the jurisdiction's footprint or responsibility looks like beyond its own boundary.

policyAnchors.description: The binding or stated commitments this dimension's target is drawn from.

status.description: Verified status as of the research date.

comparisonNote.description: How this jurisdiction differs from a peer portrait on this dimension, with both figures where known. Makes multi-city portraits worth comparing.

dataGaps.description: Specific missing data plus which agency or expert would hold it.

actions.description: 3-6 concrete, jurisdiction-specific ways residents can get involved

experts.description: Organizations to consult for indicator validation. Organizations and public contact routes only — never a private individual's personal contact details.

subIndicators.description: Additional data points for this dimension

reviewStatus.description: Provenance of the severity level and figures.

state.description: draft=assigned by a research pass, not yet checked; adversarially-reviewed=an independent reviewer re-fetched sources and applied corrections; expert-validated=confirmed by a topic expert.

geographicScaleNote.description: Free-text qualification of the geographic scale where the enum loses information (e.g. 'city (Jamaica Bay only)').
